name: Spruce Beer for Present Use
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: gallons and a half of water
ingredients.originalText: two gallons and a half of water

ingredients.name: ground white ginger
ingredients.originalText: a table-spoonful of ground white ginger

ingredients.name: essence of spruce
ingredients.originalText: a table-spoonful of essence of spruce

ingredients.name: three or four raisins per bottle
ingredients.originalText: three or four raisins per bottle

instructions.text: Boil a handful of hops in two gallons and a half of water, till they fall to the bottom
Strain the water, and when it is lukewarm, stir into it a table-spoonful of ground white ginger
Add a pint of molasses and a table-spoonful of essence of spruce
Mix the whole well together in a stone jug with half a pint of yeast
Let it ferment for a day and a half, or two days
Put it into bottles, with three or four raisins in the bottom of each, to prevent any further fermentation
It will then be fit for immediate use

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Boil a handful of hops in two gallons and a half of water, till they fall to the bottom
2. Strain the water, and when it is lukewarm, stir into it a table-spoonful of ground white ginger
3. Add a pint of molasses and a table-spoonful of essence of spruce
4. Mix the whole well together in a stone jug with half a pint of yeast
5. Let it ferment for a day and a half, or two days
6. Put it into bottles, with three or four raisins in the bottom of each, to prevent any further fermentation
7. It will then be fit for immediate use
